correctness.rationale: Explicit two-bit parity embedding recovers the parity of each coordinatewise minimum. The generated span is totally isotropic in a nondegenerate 2n-dimensional binary space, so rank is at most n. Any rank-two coordinate projection forces one fourth of its vectors into an impossible state and yields the sharp 3·2^(n−2) bound. Otherwise every rank-one projection uses either line 10 or line 11; total isotropy induces a self-orthogonal code on 10-lines, so a noncanonical family spans dimension at most n−1 and has at most 2^(n−1) vectors. An explicit three-state two-coordinate construction times arbitrary even coordinates attains equality. Exhaustive clique census for 2≤n≤5 independently corroborates the infinite proof.

value.rationale: Quantifies a sharp, dimension-uniform structural stability threshold for the unique extremizer in the newly studied two-bounded multiset Eventown setting. For every n≥2 the presence of one odd multiplicity provably removes at least one quarter of maximum admissible family size; an explicit infinite sharpness family proves the bound cannot be strengthened. This is not a routine restatement of the 2^n maximum or its equality classification.
